boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten Hope College places where students can study, create, seek guidance, gather, exercise, or spend time with art, based on current official campus sources.

cards.entity_name: Jim and Martie Bultman Student Center
cards.title: Use the Student Center as a Campus Living Room
cards.subtitle: A central gathering place beside the Pine Grove
cards.notes: Bring a small group here between commitments; tour photos document lounges, tables, organization space, and flexible program areas.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated student center with varied settings for meeting, pausing, and campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies Bultman as a dedicated student-center facility on central campus, adjacent to the Pine Grove, and documents lounges, student-organization space, and flexible program areas.
cards.access_notes: Campus facility; individual rooms or program spaces may be reserved or unavailable during scheduled activities.

cards.title: Study Among Art You Can Write On
cards.subtitle: A second-floor alcove inside Van Wylen Library
cards.notes: Settle in for focused reading, then add a respectful reflection to John Saurer’s chalkboard-surfaced sculpture before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A named library alcove combining study space, alumni artwork, and a participatory chalkboard sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: Van Wylen Library identifies the A.J. Muste Alcove as a second-floor study alcove featuring two alumni sculptures, including chalkboard-surfaced forms intended for community reflections.
cards.access_notes: Located on Van Wylen Library’s second floor; use is subject to current library building hours and policies.

cards.title: Move a Project Beyond the Laptop Basics
cards.subtitle: Multimedia tools on Van Wylen Library’s second floor
cards.notes: Bring a digital assignment here when you need specialty software, visualization tools, a Cricut Maker, a heat press, or peer guidance.
cards.short_summary: A library creation space supporting multimedia work, data visualization, fabrication tools, and peer consultations.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College states that Van Wylen Library’s second-floor Digital Media Lab provides multimedia creation tools, data-analysis and visualization software, a Cricut Maker, a heat press, and student peer consultations.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Van Wylen Library; equipment availability, assistance, and entry depend on current library operations.

cards.entity_name: David J. Klooster Center for Excellence in Writing
cards.title: Talk Through a Draft With a Student Writer
cards.subtitle: Writing support beside Van Wylen’s research help desk
cards.notes: Stop in with an assignment, outline, or draft; use a drop-in conversation or reserve time for one-on-one writing assistance.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor writing center where students can work through any stage of a project with trained peers.
cards.evidence_claim: The Klooster Center says it is located in Van Wylen Library beside the research help desk and offers students one-on-one writing assistance by drop-in or appointment.
cards.source_title: Klooster Center for Excellence in Writing | Hope College
cards.access_notes: Hope community service inside Van Wylen Library; consult the center’s current hours or appointment system before visiting.

cards.entity_name: A. Paul Schaap Science Center Atrium
cards.title: Work in the Science Center Atrium
cards.subtitle: An assignment-friendly space inside Schaap
cards.notes: Use the atrium for coursework when you are already near the science departments; the college explicitly identifies it for student study.
cards.short_summary: A documented study and assignment space within Hope’s primary science teaching and research building.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College states that the A. Paul Schaap Science Center includes an atrium where students study and work on assignments.
cards.access_notes: Academic-building space; access may follow building schedules, academic operations, and scheduled events.

cards.title: Use the Rotunda for Study or a Guest Talk
cards.subtitle: The connecting space between Martha Miller’s two wings
cards.notes: Choose the rotunda for an individual work session, or check campus programming before arriving to see whether a guest lecture is scheduled.
cards.short_summary: A central architectural junction designed to support both student study and guest lectures.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College says the Martha Miller Center’s two wings join at a rotunda where students can study or attend guest lectures.
cards.source_title: Martha Miller Center for Global Communication
cards.access_notes: Academic-building space; seating may be affected by classes, lectures, or other scheduled programming.

cards.title: Connect With CDI and Multicultural Organizations
cards.subtitle: A campus house shared by CDI and student groups
cards.notes: Visit to connect with Center for Diversity and Inclusion resources or multicultural student organizations; confirm access before dropping in.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus house serving as the shared home of CDI and multicultural student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College identifies Keppel House as the home of the Center for Diversity and Inclusion and multicultural student organizations.
cards.access_notes: Visit during current CDI availability or a scheduled student-organization activity; the building is not documented as continuously open.

cards.entity_name: DeWitt Student and Cultural Center Lower Level
cards.title: Meet Where Careers, Leadership, and Alumni Work Overlap
cards.subtitle: A collaborative environment in renovated DeWitt
cards.notes: Use the lower level when a meeting connects career planning, leadership work, or alumni engagement; verify room availability first.
cards.short_summary: A renovated collaborative setting shared by three student-facing and alumni-focused offices.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College says DeWitt’s renovated lower level opened in 2023 as a collaborative learning and meeting environment for Alumni and Family Engagement, the Boerigter Center, and the Center for Leadership.
cards.access_notes: Collaborative and office space; meetings, services, and individual rooms may require appointments or reservations.

cards.title: Fit Movement Between Classes
cards.subtitle: Student recreation across courts, track, pool, and studios
cards.notes: Bring your Hope ID and choose an available activity area; check current hours and any workout-registration requirements before going.
cards.short_summary: A student recreation facility supporting individual exercise, classes, dance, swimming, and court activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Hope College documents student use of the Dow Center’s gymnasium, dance studios, conditioning area, indoor track, racquetball courts, and pool, and states Hope students may access the facility for free.
cards.access_notes: Hope students have free access; bring campus identification and check current hours, registrations, and area-specific availability.

cards.title: Reset Your Attention With an Exhibition
cards.subtitle: Campus galleries on Columbia Avenue
cards.notes: Plan a quiet exhibition visit after the museum reopens August 28; leave large bags in the lobby and follow gallery photography rules.
cards.short_summary: An accessible campus museum where students can spend time with rotating art exhibitions outside a classroom setting.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum’s current visit page says it is closed from May 18 through August 27, reopens August 28, is fully accessible, permits limited non-flash photography, and lists free admission for its named exhibitions.
cards.access_notes: Closed for summer through August 27, 2026; scheduled to reopen August 28. Closed Sundays, Mondays, holidays, and college closures.
